_meta.title: NADA & Industry Benchmark Reference - Lead Scoring
_meta.update_cadence: Annually, when new NADA Data drops (usually mid-year) and when refreshed close-rate studies publish.
_meta.how_to_use: The score-leads skill loads this file to add an absolute benchmark layer ON TOP of the existing relative 1-10 score. Close rates benchmark each source against its source-type. Cost yardsticks are displayed as context on the NADA Benchmarks tab. Every number is editable; update the value and the citation together.

support_legend.strong: Primary source (NADA PDF) or multi-source consensus. Cite confidently.
support_legend.moderate: Single credible vendor/advisory source. Cite with caveat.
support_legend.estimate: Directional only, no single authoritative study. Label clearly in output.

close_rate_benchmarks._about: Lead-to-sale (30-day) close-rate midpoints by source-type, expressed as a fraction (0.10 = 10%). Tiers: luxury / mainstream / powersports. Mainstream = industry-blended base from the studies; luxury applies a directional uplift on first-party/internet/OEM (luxury brands rank highest in internet-lead effectiveness); powersports has NO published lead-to-sale close rate, so values are proxy-estimates derived from the auto internet-lead floor (~6%, Foureyes) adjusted by Pied Piper ILE response-effectiveness (high-ILE / Harley-type dealers skew to the top of each range; ~half of powersports dealers never phone web leads, dragging the average down). The 'estimate' support flag marks every figure that is directional rather than from a single authoritative study.

website.label: Dealer Website / Internet Leads
website.source: Foureyes 30-Day Close Rate Study 2025 (realized ~6%); Demand Local / Maritz target band 10-15%; high performers 18-20%. Luxury uplift per WardsAuto/Pied Piper internet-effectiveness rankings.

phone.label: Phone / Call-In Leads
phone.source: Urban Science / Foureyes via Demand Local: 14% 30-day close. Phone also sets appointments ~75% vs ~40% internet.

walk_in.label: Walk-In / Showroom / Floor Traffic
walk_in.source: Foureyes 2025: 25% 30-day close, highest of any source; 83.7% of those sales close in the first 3 days.

third_party.label: Third-Party Marketplace (AutoTrader, Cars.com, CarGurus, Edmunds, TrueCar)
third_party.source: Rework 2026: new-car third-party leads close 5-7%. AutoTrader sold rate ~10.9%; TrueCar ~4% standard. Mainstream-brand phenomenon; luxury relies less on these.

oem.label: OEM / Factory-Referred Leads
oem.source: Rework 2026: OEM brand-site leads close 13-15%, above generic third-party, below dealer-website first-party.

owned_equity.label: Owned Equity - Repeat / Referral / Service Drive
owned_equity.source: ESTIMATE (range 30-45%). Best-documented of the estimate buckets and the top-converting channel. AutoAlert 2026: equity-mining shown-appt-to-sold 25-30% avg, 33-38% strong, 40%+ top decile. Equity/repeat leads cited 40-50% close (Demand Local 2025). Caveat: a QUALIFIED equity/service/repeat lead closes 30-45%; a RAW whole-database mining campaign converts only ~3-10% to sale. This benchmark scores qualified leads.

chat.label: Chat / Digital-Retail Tools (Gubagoo, Podium, Roadster, CarNow, ActivEngage)
chat.source: ESTIMATE (range 10-18%, online deal-builder sub-channel skews 15-20%). Chat behaves like first-party website leads but outperforms generic web forms: Cox Automotive ~2-3x close-rate lift from chat-to-store conversation continuity; live chat +20-30% conversion vs static forms; Gubagoo early-adopter close 15% vs third-party 5-8% (2013, dated vendor data); CarNow 13.55% click-to-lead. Absolute close rates are largely vendor-derived, hence estimate. Too central to automotive to leave unscored.

data_list.label: OEM / FS Data Lists, Conquest & Equity-Mining (not buy-leads)
data_list.source: Data lists (OEM financial-services lists such as Stellantis Financial or BMW Financial Services, owner-in-market, event/tour rosters, equity-mining feeds) are names, not inbound buy-leads. Near-zero direct close is expected and correct. NOT benchmarked (vs Bench = N/A) and excluded from the store self-score; still scored 1-10 relative to this report.

store_blended._about: Reference only. The live store self-score does NOT use these fixed numbers; it computes a lead-weighted expectation from each acquisition source's own source-type benchmark, so the store is judged against its actual lead mix (an internet-only report is held to a lower bar than a walk-in-inclusive one). These fixed full-source blends are kept as a sanity-check reference (full-source scorecard: internet + phone + walk-in + owned).
store_blended.source: Mainstream 16% = Foureyes H1 2025 blended 30-day close (16.2%, 8M+ opportunities, strong). Luxury (17%) is a directional uplift and powersports (13%) is a proxy-estimate (no published powersports blend) - both directional, not from a single study.

cost_yardsticks._about: NADA cost/economics context shown on the NADA Benchmarks tab. Displayed as reference; the close-rate layer drives the benchmark flags.

ad_cost_per_new_unit_usd.source: NADA Data 2025, p.15. Up 4.8% YoY (from $705 in 2024). Blended cost-per-sale target should sit near or below this.

ad_pct_of_total_gross.source: Widely-cited NADA recommended band (not in the PDF directly). Guardrail for the annual ad-budget envelope.

ad_channel_mix_2025.source: NADA Data 2025, p.16. Digital is ~75% of total ad spend. Third-party listing sites = 20% (the marketplace line to scrutinize).

gross_per_unit_usd._about: Front+back gross per unit. NADA Data 2025 does NOT publish per-unit gross; these are Haig Partners Q2 2025 figures, store-specific and editable. The NCB model used $2,387 from that store's own June deals.
gross_per_unit_usd.source: Haig Partners - New Vehicle Gross Profits Rebound Q2 2025. Buy-sell advisory aggregate, not NADA. Override per store.

seasonal_indices_nada._about: NADA luxury/import monthly seasonal demand pattern, for annualizing a short window to a 12-month run rate. Index 1.00 = annual average month.

brand_tier_map._about: Maps a franchise keyword (matched case-insensitively in the store name) to a benchmark tier. Default tier when no keyword matches = mainstream.
